user_input.text: Build a turn-based, seeded roguelike crossing game in vanilla JavaScript, HTML and CSS, with no external assets. Each arrow-key press is exactly one turn: nothing moves except on a turn, and there is no wall clock or unseeded randomness, so the same seed and inputs always produce the same state. Floors are procedurally generated from the seed, and at least five floors escalate in difficulty. Every floor combines at least three hazard kinds whose timing interacts: patrols on fixed loops, a tide that floods and drains rows on a cycle, and tiles that collapse a set number of turns after being stepped on. Shards lengthen a body that follows the head; every segment occupies a cell and is subject to every hazard. Before a floor is shown, an in-game solver must search the time-dependent state space, including the body, prove the exit reachable, and regenerate the floor if it is not. The game displays the proven shortest solution length as par and the route itself. On the default seed, floor 1 has par at most 20 moves and a shard reachable within 12 moves. A Start / Restart button resets to the default seed. Everything needed to judge play appears as DOM text, not only on a canvas: floor, turn, position, body length, par, route, outcome and cause of death.
user_input.attribution: operator-authored task, written because the user asked for something harder ("Think of something harder"); not a player report

operational_roots.attribution: experiment-authored operational interpretations, not spontaneous model desires or additional user preferences
operational_roots.crossing: Cross generated hazard floors whose timings interact, on a route the game can prove exists.
operational_roots.growth: Acquire growth and navigate with the resulting body, every segment of which is subject to the same hazards.

feedback.text: These are source-bound observations from authored control sequences, not player preferences. Review the results against your prior expectations and the existing task, and decide what they warrant next: an artifact change, a development of meaning, retention, or abstention. None is preferred.
feedback.attribution: authored harness feedback accompanying actual observations only

criteria.crossing: From restart on the default seed, a control sequence no longer than the displayed par reaches the exit and the readout reports the floor change; repeating the sequence reproduces identical readouts; stepping into a hazard reports the defined outcome and cause.
criteria.growth: Acquiring a shard increases displayed body length by exactly one, and subsequent control-driven movement reflects the advertised body rules, including hazards applying to every segment.

unknown_rule: An unsuccessful finite search or missing observation is unknown, not proof of impossibility or unmet desire. A witnessed defect may support not_met only against the exact frozen criterion and source.
shared_consequences: Record interactions if observed; neither coupling nor a new relationship is a pass requirement. Independent games and zero-growth crossing are valid outcomes.
minimum_obligations: Preserve root identities, history and permission boundaries
excluded_claims: causal TSR advantage from one pair
stop: one completion or justified retention after each observation batch
unknown external effect or safety blocker
admission: Bound at launch to the recorded operator approval and a fresh independent binding review.

observation_policy.attribution: authored prospective tester policy; not player preference
observation_policy.discovery: Read visible instructions and current source only to map advertised controls and readouts to each root. Record source hashes, mapping and uncertainty before testing. No code edits, injected state, external assets or desired relationship supplied. Ambiguous or absent mapping is unknown, not not_met. The same blinded mapping reviewer and rules serve each arm; count mapping work as operator setup. Review records alone do not authenticate a reviewer. Existing trusted operator admission remains required, and mapping/registration setup is disclosed as operator assistance. This packet does not claim automatic mapper orchestration.
observation_policy.search: For each of the three batches, use six predeclared blind words (Up, Right, Down, Left repeated; Up Right Down Left cycled; Up Left Down Right cycled), plus one reviewed route word. Blind word length comes from the mapping's reviewed coverage declaration, fixed before any trace runs: max(12, min(32, need + 4)) inputs, where need is the batch criterion's min_inputs (doubled for the alternating mixed-pursuit batch). The route word is in the mapping (routes: crossing, growth, mixed), taken from the game's displayed route or source before any control trace runs, and independently reviewed; at most 32 inputs. Map each position by batch (crossing, growth, or alternating), preserving direction order. Each trace starts a fresh page and advertised restart, then 100ms between inputs: at most 64 native actions. Observe final DOM readouts. Execute every trace twice; retain every result, not selected successes. A route that fails is kept as a result and is not replaced. No trace segmentation or cross-probe state continuity is claimed.
observation_policy.unsupported: Analog, timing-sensitive or unmappable controls are marked partial/unknown; no claim of universal game coverage. Do not add a favorable hand-crafted route after seeing results. A different search policy requires a new predeclared observation phase applied symmetrically.
observation_policy.selection: No outputs are scored for coupling, novelty, failure or a third desire. Outcomes remain unknown until actual control traces run.
observation_policy.repeatability: Record clock/randomness conditions. Fixed controllable timing/seed is synthetic environmental input, never state injection. If source exposes no controllable seed, record nondeterminism; do not claim matched random outcomes.
observation_policy.binding: Freeze each exact source-local control/readout mapping and protected checker plan before execution. Mapping identities differ by artifact but policy and coverage are identical. A changed artifact invalidates prior source binding.
observation_policy.capacity: Two probes per supplemental bundle; seven bundles per batch including repeats, twenty-one across three batches. Existing lifetime32-admission boundary remains. Preflight actual retained admission count; do not silently truncate if insufficient. Further changed-artifact rounds require a new source-bound mapping and capacity check; absence of coverage stays unknown.
observation_policy.transport: supplemental-browser@v3 preserves original checks/state. After all bundles are registered, executed and linked, observed_supplemental_set freezes the exact chronological current receipt set per criterion. Every registered mapped bundle must have an observation. criterion-evidence@v7 exports every published mapped raw case with exact source/receipt binding. Failed, partial and unavailable observations remain present. Any missing/unavailable protocol coverage requires unknown; no automatic semantic success or human fulfillment. Existing single-receipt records retain their schema. New source or further observations require a fresh valid publication rather than silently modifying a frozen assessment.
observation_policy.orchestration_limits: Completeness is over registered/imported native observations, not an unlinked external execution. Operator-assisted orchestration must register before execution, retain and link each attempt before starting the next, and stop on unknown effects or incomplete linkage. Do not conceal adverse results by revocation: current-source revocation blocks cumulative assessment. Actual reviewer provenance, control mapping and new source identities require reviewed prospective setup; labels alone do not authenticate a reviewer.
observation_policy.coverage_gate: Before dispatch, experiments/continuous-game-v4/mapping.py runs scripts/engine-observation-coverage.py static for each batch and refuses a batch whose words cannot reach the declared min_inputs. After each batch, run the coverage tool in observed mode on the raw reports and record any invariant readout; an invariant criterion is reported as undiscriminated, never as not_met.
